title: Server sim: 20 Hz tick with 10 Hz snapshots
description: The authoritative simulation loop for a star system shard: fixed 20 Hz tick integrating ship physics via the shared flight model, queueing client inputs, and broadcasting 10 Hz entity snapshots to all connections in the system.
acceptanceCriteria: src/server/shard/sim.ts: SimLoop runs a fixed 1/20 s tick with drift correction (accumulator; max catch-up 5 ticks to avoid spiral-of-death, then drop inputs)

Each tick: drain each connected player's input queue (latest input per player wins), integrateShip (TASK-22) with server-side regime/planet context, advance entity positions; AI ships handled by a stub until TASK-46
Every 2nd tick (10 Hz): broadcast entity_update {entities: EntityState[]} to all in-system connections; snapshot includes hull/shields/target for combat-ready state
Tick timing measured per tick (histogram kept in the shard); p95 tick < 30 ms with 16 simulated ships (unit benchmark)
Input messages carry seq; the server ignores stale seq (out-of-order protection) and logs drops at debug level
Unit tests: accumulator math (no drift over 1000 ticks), latest-input-wins, stale-seq ignored, snapshot cadence exactly 10 Hz (fake timers), benchmark within budget

steps.details: src/server/shard/types.ts: Shard = {systemId, sim, connections: Map<connId, ConnState>, entities, events (EventEmitter), persist}. SimLoop class: start()/stop(), setInterval-free design using a setTimeout chain for drift correction; onTick callback.

ConnState = {playerId, lastSeq, input?: InputMsg}. WS 'input' handler enqueues. Tick: for each conn with input, integrateShip(entity, input, 1/20, regimeCtx) — regimeCtx resolves planet/heightAt from the system's generated data (cached surface chunks around the ship, radius 512 m).

Build EntityState[] (ships, characters later) each 2nd tick; serialize once, send the same buffer to all conns (ws.send with binary? keep JSON for v1, shared buffer). Track broadcast size; warn if > 32 KB (tuning input for TASK-60).
Per-tick duration into a ring-buffer histogram (p50/p95/p99). Benchmark test: 16 ships with varied inputs, 60 s simulated, assert p95 < 30 ms on the dev machine; record numbers.
All unit tests with fake timers; run lint/typecheck/test. Note: a real multi-client integration test arrives with TASK-70.

technicalNotes: This sim runs against a test-only single shard for now; TASK-11 introduces the router that creates/reaps shards. Keep the Shard interface clean — the router will instantiate it.
All entity mutation happens only inside onTick (single writer) — message handlers only enqueue. This invariant is what keeps the sim deterministic and debuggable.
heightAt lookups must be O(1): cache the 3x3 chunk neighborhood per ship per tick.
